gaps.sentence: The author ___ books sell millions worldwide lives in Iceland.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the author to her books; 'who' could not be followed directly by 'books'.

gaps.sentence: It was the best meal ___ I have ever eaten.
gaps.hint: after a superlative, this pronoun is preferred
gaps.explanation: After superlatives ('the best ...'), 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, ___ attracts millions of visitors, was completed in 1889.
gaps.explanation: For things in non-defining clauses use 'which'; 'that' is not allowed after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The restaurant ___ we had dinner last night has excellent reviews.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' after place nouns; no preposition appears in the clause.

gaps.sentence: The moment ___ she saw the results, she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'When' links the moment to the action; 'where' and 'why' do not fit a time noun.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.
